summary: Elizabeth Morrison works in Buddhist studies and sinology. She studied under doctoral supervisors Bernard Faure and Carl Bielefeldt and teachers Janet Gyatso and Susan Niditch. She held posts at Amherst College (1998–1999) and Middlebury College (attested 2008).

Elizabeth Napper is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Virginia, studying under Paul Groner, Jeffrey Hopkins, and Geshe Wangyal. She served as co-director of the Tibetan Nuns Project (attested 2001–2006).

Elke Rogersdotter specializes in Indology and history/archaeology. She completed her PhD at Umeå University (attested 2006), studying under Bozena Werbart and Thomas B. Larsson, alongside co-advisors Karin Viklund and P. Ajithprasad.
Ellen M. Raven is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. She held positions at Leiden University, attested there in 2003 and on the Editorial Board in 2018.
Elliot M. Stern is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He pursued his graduate studies at the University of Pennsylvania, where he was a doctoral candidate until 1988 and received his PhD in 1998.

Elliot Sperling (1951–2017) was a scholar in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He studied at Queens College and Indiana University (PhD ~1983) under Helmut Hoffmann and Lynn A. Struve. He held posts at Indiana University (~1987–2015) and Harvard University.

Ellison Banks Findly specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology, and studied under Fred Pfeil. She has held posts at Mount Holyoke College and Trinity College, where she was an associate professor of religion and Asian studies (attested 1989).
Emanuela Garatti is a Tibetologist. She has held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (attested 2018).

Embar Krishnamacharya was an Indologist. He held posts at the Oriental Research Institute and Manuscripts Library as a pandit, at Sanskrit Pathashala, Vadtal (attested 1937), and at Baroda College (attested 1939).

Emi Matsushita (b. 1970) specializes in history/archaeology and Japanology. She studied at Nanzan University, the University of East Anglia, and Ohio State University under John C. Huntington. She held posts at Shizuoka Prefectural Board of Education and Ohio State University.

Emil Rödiger (1801–1874) was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He studied at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1821–1825), where he later held a post (~1826–1853), before holding an appointment at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1853–1874).

Emil Sieg (1866–1951) was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Kiel and Humboldt University of Berlin, and held professorships at Berlin (1896–1908), Kiel (~1909–1920), and Göttingen (~1920–1935).

Emilio Teza (1831–1912) was an Italian scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied under Anton Boller. He held academic posts at the University of Bologna (~1860–1872), the University of Pisa (~1872–1886), and the University of Padua (~1886–1912).

Emily T. Yeh (b. 1971) specializes in Tibetology. She studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology and the University of California, Berkeley, and held a post at the University of Colorado Boulder (~2003).

Emmie te Nijenhuis (b. 1931) is an Indologist. She studied at the Utrecht School of the Arts and Utrecht University, where she completed her PhD in 1970. She later held a post at the University of Amsterdam.

Enamul Haque (1937–2022) was a scholar of history/archaeology and Indology. He completed his studies at the University of Dhaka (~1957–1962) and the University of Oxford (~1969–1973), and held a long-term post at Bangladesh National Museum (~1962–1991).

Encho Tamura (1917–2013) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, history/archaeology, and Japanology. Educated at Kyoto and Kyushu universities, he held professorships at Kyushu and Kumamoto universities, and directed the Kyushu Historical Museum and Fukuoka Prefectural Human Rights Center.

Endo Asai (1927–2004) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1946–1949). He served as a director at Rissho University (~1958–1998), president of Minobusan University (~1997–2004), and held a post at Nihon Fukushi University.
Eng Jin Ooi specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a PhD from Mahidol University in 2021, where his doctoral supervisors were Giuliano Giustarini, Peter Skilling, and Kengo Harimoto.
Enga Teramoto (1872–1940) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts as a lecturer at Kyoto University (~1908–1923) and as a professor at Otani University (1915).
